proposed_adr.title: Proposed: Present investigation terminal states as a brief table in docs/INVESTIGATE.md
proposed_adr.context: The investigation documentation defines two success terminal states, ready_for_decision and needs_input. They differ by whether any blocking question remains and both return decision_approved:false and delivered:false. Human acceptance, Jira export and delivery admission are separate future actions. Today the states are described in prose. Assumptions, none of them in the registered excerpt: operators scan the section more than they read it end to end, GitHub-flavored Markdown tables render correctly, and lines 60-96 are the only place the states are described. This proposal changes documentation only, under docs/, and changes no runtime, persistence, security, API, concurrency or deployment behavior. It is a proposal only and is not an approval.
proposed_adr.decision: Proposed: replace the prose for the two terminal states with a two-row table with state, condition and flags columns. The ready_for_decision row says no blocking question remains. The needs_input row says a blocking question remains. Both rows state decision_approved:false and delivered:false. Add one sentence after the table saying that human acceptance, Jira export and delivery admission are separate future actions and that neither state is an approval. Keep the statement that unverified external claims remain assumptions or open questions.
proposed_adr.consequences: Operators can compare the two states at a glance. The risk of reading a state as approval or delivery is reduced as long as the table keeps the condition, both flags and the separate-future-actions sentence. The docs now depend on Markdown table rendering. The wording can drift from the controller behavior and needs a manual consistency check against the excerpt. No runtime change results. Human review is still required before any adoption, and this ADR has not been approved, exported or delivered.

proposed_adr.consequences: Operators can compare the two states at a glance. The risk of reading a state as approval or delivery is reduced as long as the table keeps the condition, both flags and the separate-future-actions sentence. The docs now depend on Markdown table rendering. The wording can drift from the controller behavior and needs a manual consistency check against the excerpt. No runtime change results. Human review is still required before any adoption, and this ADR has not been approved, exported or delivered.
proposed_adr.context: The investigation documentation defines two success terminal states, ready_for_decision and needs_input. They differ by whether any blocking question remains and both return decision_approved:false and delivered:false. Human acceptance, Jira export and delivery admission are separate future actions. Today the states are described in prose. Assumptions, none of them in the registered excerpt: operators scan the section more than they read it end to end, GitHub-flavored Markdown tables render correctly, and lines 60-96 are the only place the states are described. This proposal changes documentation only, under docs/, and changes no runtime, persistence, security, API, concurrency or deployment behavior. It is a proposal only and is not an approval.
proposed_adr.decision: Proposed: replace the prose for the two terminal states with a two-row table with state, condition and flags columns. Add one sentence after the table saying that human acceptance, Jira export and delivery admission are separate future actions and that neither state is an approval. Keep the statement that unverified external claims remain assumptions or open questions.
